package_info.package_manager: N/A (core infrastructure, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to PR 81056 / issue #1711 fix
package_info.why_malicious: A race condition vulnerability in Kubernetes allowed nodes with duplicate hostnames to overwrite each other's state in etcd, leading to cluster instability and potential denial of service. While not a traditional 'malicious package', this logic flaw could be exploited by an attacker with node-joining privileges to disrupt or crash the cluster.

required_permissions: ability to set hostname or use --hostname-override

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
etcd key: /registry/minions/HOSTNAME
# HOSTNAME is not enforced to be unique
# Each node update overwrites the same key if hostnames are duplicated
malicious_snippets.code_language: Go (Kubernetes core logic, conceptual etcd key usage)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a node joins the cluster, it registers its state under /registry/minions/HOSTNAME in etcd. If two nodes share the same hostname, each update overwrites the same key, causing a race condition and cluster instability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing multiple nodes to register with the same hostname enables a race condition that can be triggered intentionally to disrupt cluster operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, each node should have a unique identifier in the cluster state store. Allowing duplicate hostnames violates this expectation and undermines cluster integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be a node rejoining after a reboot, but not multiple active nodes with the same name.
key_indicators: No uniqueness check on node hostname during join
Cluster instability and high CPU load on master

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a node is started with --hostname-override set to an existing node's hostname, it registers under the same etcd key, causing the same race condition and instability.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The --hostname-override flag can be abused to intentionally create duplicate node identities, triggering the vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, --hostname-override is used for legitimate renaming, not for duplicating existing node identities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Used in cloud environments to set a custom node name, but not to duplicate an existing one.
key_indicators: Use of --hostname-override with a duplicate value
Multiple nodes reporting the same hostname

attack_chain.action: Attacker provisions a new node and sets its hostname (or uses --hostname-override) to match an existing node in the cluster.
attack_chain.leads_to: Node joins cluster with duplicate identity.

attack_chain.action: Both nodes periodically update their state in etcd under the same key (/registry/minions/HOSTNAME), causing a race condition.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cluster state becomes unstable; master node experiences high CPU load.

attack_chain.action: Cluster instability escalates, potentially leading to denial of service or crash of the master node.

behavioral_signatures: Multiple nodes reporting the same hostname in cluster state
Frequent overwrites of the same etcd key (/registry/minions/HOSTNAME)
Unusual spike in master node CPU usage after node join events
network_indicators: Multiple nodes with the same hostname communicating with the master
Repeated registration requests from different IPs with the same node name
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor etcd for frequent updates to the same /registry/minions/HOSTNAME key from different node IPs. Alert if multiple nodes report the same hostname or if --hostname-override is used with a value matching an existing node. Investigate spikes in master node CPU usage following node join events.
